header: Thirteen years of the Anbach network
lead: The institute started with eleven masts and a spreadsheet. What follows is the short version — the long one is in the twentieth anniversary report.

entries.title: Eleven stations go live
entries.text: The first masts are installed between Talhof and the weir, funded for three years and expected to be dismantled afterwards.

entries.title: The series becomes public
entries.text: Readings move from an internal spreadsheet to an open portal. Within a month a secondary school is using them in class, which settles the question of whether anyone outside the institute wanted them.

entries.title: Forty-six masts, and the first full winter without a gap
entries.text: Local storage on every station closes the outages that had made January unusable for five years running.

entries.title: The raw series is published alongside the checked one
entries.text: Not a popular decision internally. It has since become the reason most external users say they trust the corrected figures.

entries.title: The refit
entries.text: One specification for every mast, chosen so that a failed part can be swapped from a van rather than ordered.

entries.title: The warmest summer on record
entries.text: Eleven consecutive days above 21 degrees at the three shallow stations, and the first year the network was dense enough to show where it started.
